notes.title: Update 1.8.1
notes.content:
Hello everyone. As promised, this is our May update. Our apologies for only a couple fixes, but we felt necessary to post what we have done so far. Our development has been underwhelming lately, made it worse with our subversion being disabled by tragic circunstances. We hope Xp-Dev's main developer's family recover from the loss of a dear family member.

Since we are disallowed to use it, our updates and files have been transferred manually, which increases our time drastically. Internally, we decided to let our subversion client resolve their internal issues while we develop our campaign.

Though we are behind in programming, our artwork and animation has been going fast. We have a script ready and expect everyone to like this small preamble to our main campaign, as a prelude that is actually an epilogue. You'll guys know more details in a few.

Not everything is bad news. Hyperkinetic has been a great partner so far with us and now has most of the knowledge of our code. This will help in the future with faster updates, but it'll require the subversion client to be restored. I hope everyone has a nice weekend!


Fixes:

* Some units were having a red glow when attacked (Visigoth units) others aren't (Frankish units like Trustismanne and Galikakus)

* Units were playing both Hurt and Defeat animations when defeated; should go direct to Defeated

notes.title: Update 1.8
notes.content:
Hello, everyone. Today we give our Christmas present to everyone who contributes to our game. Its been several months since our last endeavours in developing were made, and we can safely say that the first fruits arrived in time for the holidays. 

A long-remaining glitch in our multiplayer code left everyone without the means to play with each other, which was one of the core features of our early builds. As much as desync and bugs still happened, it was possible for players to play freely by creating a room and inviting others for a fight. Today, this has been finally addressed, and our partners at Hyperkinetic worked hard to provide a fix. This has revealed as well that our current code is not up to standards (evidenced by our previously mentioned problems), and not only has the fix been made, but we are now aware of the steps required to upgrade our systems for larger scale playing. Its not realistic for us to make this change right now, as we shifted our focus to single player, but its definately on our radar on things to-do once campaigns are fully implemented.

The update is not without content, tho. We made several grammar mistakes on item descriptions, tweaked a few weapons and added a new type of Long Sword, the Semispatha. Players now can choose between the Hairus, the Spatha and Semispatha as their weapon of choice, each with their own advantages and disadvantages. 

Progress on the campaign side will remain constant as we slowly but surely add the content required for implementation. Because it takes some time for programmers to understand previous work, the inertia is now broken, and you can expect more constant updates throughout the next year.

* Added: New Long Sword-class item, the Semispatha. A sword that is light and fast, and even cheaper than other models, but has slightly reduced damage and Parry value due to its lower reach.

* Fixed: Multiplayer should now work again. Desync issues and bugs related to turn order and units should still happen, albeit at a reduced amount due to code optimization.

* Fixed: Grammatical mistakes on several item descriptions.

* Fixed: Brunjo armor had the same pricing as Lorica Hamata.

* Fixed: Several units should walk/run in a less realistic, but faster pace, slightly reducing wait times between moves. This should happen more often in new updates.

notes.title: A Change of Roads (Campaigns)
notes.content:
Hello there. When we started Rise of the Foederati, we envisioned a project that would begin as a multiplayer experience first, and a single-player campaign game second. The objective was to build a historical game where players could travel around and seek adventure with their tribes and play along with their friends for objectives, fun or even just competitively seek to outpace other players in the same tribe. Our team begun very small, with an artist, programmer, game support designer/developer; then came an accountant, new artists, support programmers, and we started hiring voice actors to play the leaders and the trailers. Development was good; in 2017, we showed how our project was coming along in local game fairs, such as Brasil Game Show, together with other indie games. It was a great pleasure to be standing next to indie big names such as Knights of Pen and Paper devs, for example, and we managed to talk and have great suggestions and criticism for how the game looked.

The most common criticism we had from most players was our lack of single-player support. This is evidence in multiple forum discussions we had showcasing our product, where people would rather play with their own pace and learn more about the game first, before diving in a multiplayer mode. In a strategy game, this makes sense, as players first want to know mechanics, combos and efficient tactics first, before putting them to the test against others. 

As it is understood, our game was initially sold with multiplayer sessions in mind. But because so many people are longing for a full campaign, we are very excited to announce the shift in our development direction! instead providing several campaigns of varied difficulty that put the tribes that we already developed in a story with multiple episodes. This means you as a player will get to play against a more difficult, smarter AI in a series of challenges across different landscapes, battles and political troubles that can shift according to your own decisions. Below is the detailed list of our changes for the future:

[list]
[*] Multiplayer efforts are now put second to single player. We are hanging gears to develop a cutscene editor to a multi-episode single-player campaign featuring events that happened after Rise of the Foederati's timeline, but very similar in setting. More details to come.

[*] The new planned units are on hold until we manage to fix a critical bug in the new units' animators, developed to fit all animations that are needed for a more complex graphical showing of their equipment in-game. 

[*] The new tribe, the Alans, are planned and set to return to the development phase once we manage to finish our campaign. Eventually, they will also get their own campaign, and its our expectations that each tribe has their own leader or important figure to have their own. This is a slight change as well from our historical accuracy perspective; several tribes do not have legendary or historical figures in Rise of the Foederati, while others have too many; we will try to feature as many important names as possible and add theoretical, fictional elements that tie together with real historical happenings.

[*] Many people purchased our game because of our multiplayer focus-first, and are waiting for a long time for our product to be finished. We are checking how to open a refund program for those that feel like the change of pace in development does not suit their waiting anymore.

[*] Until the end of the year, no new updates are programmed, but we will now update players more often with news of this change.
[/list] 

We listened, and because this ties so well with providing content with more haste without compromising quality (because of the lessened complexity), expect to hear from us again soon. Our first campaign features one of the greatest Visigoth heroes of all time, whose actions profoundly changed the world at the time. We cannot wait to share more details! Last but not least, we do not plan on ditching multiplayer entirely; there are discussions ongoing for how we can implement episodes with two-player options.

notes.title: New units, tribe, animations and regarding maps
notes.content:
Hi there.

It's been a while since our last update. We didn't give you guys a Merry Christmas nor a Happy New Year, but we've been hard at work to provide something to make up for this. Our timeline is filled with holes and not complete yet for this year, because of many not-listed-before content being added. 

Taking into a bulletpoint list, lets address each point here.

[list]
[*] New units.

Until the end of February-mid March, all tribes will feature their six Ordinary units and one Authority unit, meaning the remaining tribes, Basques and Franks, will have their new units added. The Frankish unit should take longer because of the sheer amount of animations and its new depiction of a mechanic regarding reloading weapons. 

After this, our focus will go into the new tribe. The new tribe ready, we'll add a new leader for each tribe, making it possible for players to choose one of the two tribe units, each with strengths and weaknesses.

[*] New tribe.

The Alans, Alani, or Alanians, are the new tribe to be added. We do not have a preview of when it should be ready, but consider it a priority for us in 2022. Their playstyle will be very different from the rest of the tribes, with heavy focus on cavalry and using foot units as supportive roles, instead of the other way around.

[*] New animations.

All units that can switch weapons will have a fast, but noticeable animation of them sheathing/putting away their last weapon and drawing their new. Below an example and preview of our new Frankish unit.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/5e137bf24e9ab96ea6c9b41ba41a9f6f7e3bb450.gif[/img]

This should be ready and uploaded in a new patch by the end of February.

[*] Map travelling/new game modes

This is our main programming focus, and it is incredibly painful to pull it off because its almost a new game on of itself. Too many variables to consider and the fact its a multiplayer scene that is shared with hundreds of players per server makes it difficult for us to nail it. There is no ETA for its conclusion, but maybe a test server for strain testing will be needed. Once the basics are set, we can start creating new game modes. 
[/list]

This should be for now, so expect a new patch until the end of the next month and more content soon. Our apologizes for the long silence.

notes.title: Update 1.7.0
notes.content:
Hello everyone, it's been a while.

We apologize for the four-month silence, work has been hectic in all fronts. There are many things to correct and many things to add to our game, and this update tries to bring forth all our work in this time period to fruition. Most possibly, this update surpasses all others in relation to content. We have new units coming along in the next weeks, a whole lot of abilities that more than double the last amount. And there are also many fixes to bugs.

Unfortunately, all this does not take away the fact that we are late in several of our timeline milestones. We said we were eager to provide map conquest support for gameplay that gets closer to our general game idea, and this update does not provide it, yet. Instead, we continue to build the foundations for a more complete gameplay when the first template for this game mode is complete. As always, we greatly appreciate your patience and your continuous support in our project. There is always a looming threat hanging on the heads of supporters of early access titles that stay silent for a long time, and we're once again here to dispel this possibility. Delays are part of all game development processes, and this is not an exception. 

To better address those who purchased the early access title, a new timeline is going to be updated for a new revision, explaining in more details which parts are ready, which are underdevelopment, those that are delayed until further notice and others that are in the pipeline queue.

Last but not least, you saw in our May news the new units. They will start being available to each tribe starting in this update, with the Visigoths now gaining a Medium Infantry unit, the Haralauhts (Swordsman). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/12eebac61af911674c8d7366c0a1f6c1a4ef06ec.png[/img]

This soldier is a head-on warrior that has abilities fit for either smart duelling or shredding lighter units with both brawn and strength. 

The other three tribes will gain units that are more flavorful towards their playstyle, as well, and will serve to solidify their identity in the game.

Finally, below are the patch notes for Update 1.7.0. There will be more regular updates after this one to add the new units, as well as new content, such as new maps, and possibly the new game mode. To make testing easier, once the travelling is better, you'll be able to join the test server to check how it works. 

[b]Fixes[/b]

[list]
[*]Breaking error when attempting to list inventory settings that included a deleted item.
Invalid unit animation states machine mapping resulting in units unable to play animations that were meeting their conditions.
[*]Spikes when fetching the owner unit of a state machine for the first time, thus leading to some frames to be skipped; all units and their animators are cached on startup for better animation performance.
[*]Comparison of the unit by memory reference was failing even if it was the same physical unit, it now compares by ID throughout the game.
[*]Some animators had the wrong idle state names and thus struggling to change the state properly.
[*]Breaking error when generating a unit with deleted initial equipment/inventory items.
[*]Attack Chain Points were going negative if consumption were higher than the current value.
[*]Breaking error when viewing an ability tree that had an ability that no longer exists.
[*]Breaking error when searching for an icon for an opinion range that's obsolete.
[*]Retaliations were not costing the proper stamina cost bonus.
[*]Incorrect movement stamina penalty based on unit mount or class.
[*]Some passive effects were applied to the same unit multiple times if it moves in and out of the effect range.
[*]Opinions were forced to clamp to (0:100) when there were opinions that scaled down to -100.
[*]A bug where damage reduction and absorption were reversed when applied to damage.
[*]Square Average of some effects was 0 due to one of the effects is 0, resulting in others being neglected.
[*]All abilities had effects that were specific only to certain abilities.
[*]No morale was applied for an attacker with a successful attack with no damage.
[*]Breaking error when attempting to defeat an already defeated unit with multi attacks like Overwhelm.
[*]Command ability effects with different distances were applied to all units within the max distance.
[*]Movement stamina cost was consumed for the entire path even though the unit may get interrupted on the way.
[*]Some abilities had the wrong setup, for example, Quick Swing was ignoring accuracy instead of parry.
[*]Some passives were having the wrong ability type.
[*]Some abilities were free to unlock/level/use when they shouldn't.
[/list]



[b]Changes[/b]

[list]
[*]Ability cooldowns are now level-based.
[*]Removed unnecessary obsolete libraries causing in-build issues.
[*]Random number generator in all systems to provide less recurring values in small ranges.
[*]Defending chances are now separate rolls from the attack roll (misses should be less frequent, but [*]defenses should occurr more; this means units becoming more tired has a bigger effect in longer [*]drawn-out fights, when accuracy remains more consistent but defenses drop sharply).
[*]Attacks have specific attacker and defender stats, removing the possibility of an attack providing a willpower bonus by mistake, for example.
[*]Stamina Cost is no longer a stat, this fixes and removes confusion between effects that cost stamina and effects that require stamina.
[/list]


[b]Additions[/b]

[list]
[*]Support for equipment-specific toggles to automatically switch off if the requirement is invalidated.
[*]Support for ability-specific animations like Shield Bash.
[*]Item Kind Attribute for example short and longbows are all just bows.
[*]The new unit effect places on the unit's body (Aura Base and Parry Effect).
[*]Support for equipment-based animation states, not just for weapons, for example, there are units [*]now that have animations when equipping a quiver, an empty quiver, or no quiver at all.
[*]Better unit animation state machine mapping, allowing
[*]Support for tuning in and out of shield wall state without breaking shield wall.
[*]Shieldwall blocking.
[*]Shieldwall formations, allowing unit groups to form shield walls if next to each other in a certain pattern.
[*]Support for weapon switching animations, these are animations that show the unit drawing the new weapon instead of immediate idle animation. A few units currently do not have this on, expect them to be added in the future.
[*]Support for applying accuracy penalty to opportunity attacks.
[*]Hamstrung stacks: disabling units movements and reduces movement range.
[*]Support for leader Instruction abilities, consisting of a permanent buff at the beginning of battle for one single unit until combat ends:
[*]Instructed units can trigger automatic attacks if they and the instructor are engaged to the same target and one attacks it.
[*]Instructions can be disabled based on units’ opinions of each other, which means opinions are now effective in battle.
[*]If either participator in the instruction is defeated, the other loses any bonus morale.
[*]Some instructions may provide different effects, such as immunity against negative effects like Stun/Fumble/Disorient, dealing true damage instead of the target's HP is at a certain % (robbing lives of enemies) or evenprovide bonus movement range and disallow bonus stamina cost when running.
[*]Leader Plans: A global buff to all units that lasts until the end of combat; these are two-edged, as they provide also a penalty for units, making them be more unidimensional in combat and planning. 
[*]Bonus chances to avoid disengagement AOO.
[*]Accuracy penalty on disengagement AOO.
[*]Plans are abilities cast on the entire tribe units, changing plans is not possible except using the Change Plans plan.
[*]Brothers-in-arms bonus damage and accuracy when attacking targets that are engaged with teammates.
[*]Commander Unit Classes: commanding effects that passively apply to certain unit classes.
[*]Slayer Unit Classes: Passive effects granted to units that learn these abilities specifically making them more deadly against a unit class.
[*]Effects that alter the attack accuracy or damage mid calculation like Twisting Stabs.
[*]Effects over time from attacking like Striking Combinations.
[*]Effect to override an attack's damage and or stamina cost situationally.
[*]Movement range Effects to the unit's window.
[*]Effects that are able to deplete an attacker's ACP if the defender successfully parries an attack.
[*]Effects that instantly disable a target's Reactives (Faceslash, Advancing Parries).
[*]Effects that modify a unit's Max HP/Stamina during the battle.
[*]Effects that modify a unit's opinion of another during battle, like Camaraderie.
[*]Effects that instantly defeat the target if its hp is below a certain percent.
[*]Effects that allow units to swap positions.
[*]Effects that allow units to redirect projectile attacks from adjacent squares to self (redirected attacks are automatically covered, as of now).
[*]Effects that allow units to anticipate projectiles by being more reflexive.
[*]Effects that disallow missed projectile attacks to hit bystanders.
[*]Effects that convert an attack's damage to true damage.
[*]Effects that use equipment weight as damage (for example using shield weight in bashing).
[*]Effects that stun on critical or fumble on hit.
[*]Effects that freeze morale loss for a number of turns.
[*]Attacks that are followed by automatic Free Kicks.
[*]Attacks that use custom strength % in damage calculation.
[*]Attacks that trigger friendly AOO on target if they critically hit.
[*]Free kicks that are reducible in true damage by the target's armor.
[*]Support for random morale reduction resistance like Military Discipline (this is a huge change that resulted in all morale effects in the game are calculated by the server now).
[*]UI display of bonus notes regarding a stat/attribute effect, for example: whether or not the effect is for/against certain attacks/units classes.
[*]UI messaging of ability and stat effects should provide a clearer battle log (increasing messages over time).
[/list]

Effects that instantly defeat the target if its hp is below a certain percent.
Effects that allow units to swap positions.
Effects that allow units to redirect projectile attacks from adjacent squares to self (redirected attacks are automatically covered, as of now).
Effects that allow units to anticipate projectiles by being more reflexive.
Effects that disallow missed projectile attacks to hit bystanders.
Effects that convert an attack's damage to true damage.
Effects that use equipment weight as damage (for example using shield weight in bashing).
Effects that stun on critical or fumble on hit.
Effects that freeze morale loss for a number of turns.
Attacks that are followed by automatic Free Kicks.
Attacks that use custom strength % in damage calculation.
Attacks that trigger friendly AOO on target if they critically hit.
Free kicks that are reducible in true damage by the target's armor.

notes.title: The Road Ahead, our Timeline and Announcing the New Tribe
notes.content:
Hello there.

It's been a while since we talked about the development of the game, and instead we posted our last few updates with mostly fixes, small additions and changes to the overall balance of combat in the game. 

One of our main concerns regarding the game is transparency, and it was our decision to make a timeline where we make our predictions for our development process and lay out a comprehensive way to tell players what our goals are.

Currently, as our timeline stands, we made progress in lots of areas which were not predicted there, but lacked in others that were made there and are not ready yet. Below we detail the development points where we are late and explain to you why, and how we are going to solve it:

2020
* June: Estabilishment of ranked play and support for territory conquest

[b]This is our number one priority right now for development.[/b] We are lacking only one map as texture to finish a several provinces, where players can travel and interact with cities and each other in the same municipality. We wanted to make a different map for each city in the world, but its a far-fetched goal, now that we calculated roughly more than 800 (!) municipalities. We might make several layouts and change them slightly and distribute across all of them, as a way to portray uniqueness to them. 

Ranked play is tough, because we do not have a large enough consistent player base for it, and might not have it for some time. Its not in our plans to make players wait for hours in a queue until other player logs in. We decided, however, to use an ELO system adapted for our needs and make every game season reset the scores. The top players get rewards in the form of in-game permanent skin unlocks, some reserved for the seasons, only.

We believe that once territory conquest as a game mode is ready, it will bring a breath of fresh air into our game and portray a much more accurate view of our plans for our game. 

* July: Minigames

We have several ready to be launched once territory conquest is available.

* December: New tribe voted by the community

Thank you all for voting. Our poll was a success and the most voted tribe was the Alans, and will be the new tribe to be implemented in the game, the fifth. We are focused right now in finding artists to aid our current ones to draw the new soldiers, and once they are ready, we estimate roughly one and a half months to animate them all and implement them in the game. We might speed up the implementation with only four or five soldiers if we lag much more on this.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/363410d1cb4a29bea173b8936aaecb8b11d3114c.png[/img]

2021
* February: Tournaments 

We expected to have a base of players by then, but the problem of making ranked play also applies here. Being easier than having ranked play, this may be an easier milestone to finish than the June 2020 ones; the plan is to mix in territory conquest and tournament play, in a more dynamic ranked play-type.

* March-June: New tribes and soldiers

Judging by our current development speed, we are sorry to inform our players that [b]it is not realistic in our budget right now to create this type of content.[/b] This does NOT mean we will not make more tribes or soldiers anymore, but that our development focus has changed due to a combination of financial misfortunes. Its not in our minds to lay blame on others; the marketing and sales of our product has suffered greatly, and its on our minds to change it and make the product more profitable, so we have the funds to keep paying for development. It is important for players to note that Rise of the Foederati is entirely funded by two men and developed by another who are passionate about it and aim to create a wonderful gaming experience for all, but as human beings have families and priorities that shift according to how much they can keep funding out of their pockets this vision.

As a transparency note, we'd like everyone to know that ever since we started developing the game in 2017, our efforts have not diminished, and will not, regardless of how much our sales are a part of the funding of its development; and as the main developer of the game, I fully disclose that the entirety of the game's sales profits are going, and will go entirely into the development of our game, until it is able to fund itself entirely. Not a single cent is being withdrawn to me or any partner involved in the project for personal use. Many projects in the past have been plagued by misuse of indie games' sales figures, and one of our main concerns is to dispel such possibilities from the minds of any person who purchased or aims to purchase our game.

As said before, we talked about the points we missed in our timeline. Below are the points we managed to conclude:

* The Franks
* Bug and code cleanup
* New soldiers (August)
* The Suebians
* 2v2 Battles
* New soldiers (November)

And below are points we developed in our game without direct mention from our timeline:

* Item quality system
* Unit customization through abilities/stats
* Market trading
* Dialogue system with soldiers
* Traits

It is a great pleasure to have you all with us during our journey to a full release. Our efforts are rewarded by you guys being so considerate and patient with us. In the next months, we will release a new timeline with these changes, appointing what we managed to conclude and what we didn't, and our new plans for the future.

Hi there. Did you get tired of getting fixes? Hope not, because we will keep fixing things and adding things until you wish we didn't!!

As previously, we still are animating the new units, so no new soldiers for now.

[*] Fixed: Second attack on chain is not accounting extra stamina cost (only found on Quick attacks)
[*] Changed: Attack chain stamina cost multipliers.
[*] Changed: Javelins' Critical Hit chance reduced from 10% to 5%.
[*] Changed: Medium Armor should now be more effective at reducing damage.
[*] Added: Pause/Continue offline game shortcut (Spacebar).
[*] Added: Music tones based on the win/defeat type of the battle.
[*] Added: Warband Power attribute, a hidden attribute calculated by the overall levels of your units in your Warband and the classes they have. Units with higher pay have higher power levels than those with lower pay but the same level. Your deployed units follow this same calculation.
[*] Added: Heroic win and Humiliating defeat 
   - You get a Heroic Win if your win a battle when outnumbered 3 to 1 or more, OR if the enemy's deployed power is twice or more of your own. If you, instead, outnumber the enemy, but his deployed power is STILL twice or more than your own deployed units, then the results will never be Heroic Wins. Similarly, if you lose to an enemy which achieved a Heroic Win, you will get a Humiliating Defeat.
   - You get NO end-of-battle experience if you suffer a Humiliating Defeat (units still develop their skills, though). If you get a Heroic Win, you get half of the experience your enemy would get normally for his defeat. (Example: If the win was not Heroic, and would be a Clear Victory; you'd get 100xp and your enemy 50xp. This means if the victory is Heroic, your units get 125xp, and your enemy gets NO end-battle experience).
[/b][/list]

notes.title: Update 1.6
notes.content:
Hey guys. Today we introduce to you the last update before we add more units to all tribes, and later, add our new tribe to the mix. All new soldiers should add more layers of complexity to warband compositions, but will change little in the grand scheme of things. The list of changes are below:

[list]
[*]Added: open ability tree button to level up window. 
[*]Added: Unintended attacks count for the battle statistics.
[*]Added: Tooltip info for defense stats if they’re affected by proficiency of said defense and willpower+fatigue. 
[*]Added: current/max values to the unit in-battle bars.
[*]Added: A check before attempting to start/join a battle to test the eligibility of the warband for deployment (ex: there's at least one deployable leader).
[*]Added: Dedicated temporary morale effects. 
Effects that scar the unit like when it receives an attack/critical hit are not displayed since they affect the unit's morale until the battle's end.
If the unit has a morale gain/loss avoidance buffer it'll appear in the tooltip. 
Also visible when hovering morale in the stat list (during battle) Test
[*]Added: A check of whether or not steam save is enabled (at all) and enabled (for rise), the game will prompt if it's not enabled in your steam settings.
[*]Added: Dialogue choice pages, as better indicator of whether or not more choices are available Test
[*]Added: missing and/or incorrect win/loss messages in battles after conclusion Added: Order stats' effects by their +/- and add separator, note that for fatigue, the - effects are green(considered positive).
[*]Added: Unit health/stamina/fatigue bars on the units slots.
[*]Added: An indicator for currently hovered tile on the ground.
[*]Added: Seriously hurt units (HP <= 10%) will now appear bleeding, making it easier to know who to attack.
[*]Added: The defeat reason of a unit when hovering it's defeated icon in warband, be it surrendered/collapsed etc..
[*]Added: If the target is engaged with more than one unit, there is a bonus 10% accuracy, that bonus is instead 25% if the target is flanked from behind and the attacker didn't attack this turn.
[*]Added: Confirmation prompt before surrendering. 
[*]Added: Action improvement:
Each unit remembers it's last action that it attempts (move/attack).
Units fallback to move action in raiding.
Basic attacks shortcuts are visible by default.
Attacks buttons are grouped in one place now.
[*]Added: End Raiding Button for ability to end before timeout.
[*]Added: New defense XP gain mechanic:
Units gain up to 20 xp points for each defense per round.
The gained xp when using a defense is halved each time the defense is used in that round.
* Unit gains 10 xp for the first block (or any defense), then 5, then 2.5 until the round ends, then back to 10.
Each defense has its own gained and max gainable values.
For each defense type, the unit can gain up to a maximum of xp points that is equal to the required xp to level the defense in current level.
For example if the unit's block level progress is 99/100, the unit can gain a max 100 block points in this battle.
Another example if the unit's block level progress is 100/150 the unit can gain a max of 150 block points in this battle.
Gained defense xp is applied after battle.
[*]Added: Random deploy button. Test
[*]Added: Indicator text for when AI is thinking.
[*]Added: Permanent unit outline for enemy units if playing vs same tribe as yours or team mode. 
[*]Added: Deployment Formations system.

[b]Improvements[/b]

[*]Changed: Units will now only store data about their learnt abilities/traits instead of all in the tree (less downloading time in lobbies).
[*]Changed floating text behavior and weight.
[*]Changed: Level up button will be disabled if the unit has no more level ups.
[*]Changed: No combat experience is gained/lost if battle is discontinued before it starts (ex: leaving during deployment).
[*]Changed: changing equipment during looting is no longer allowed, since the unit will still move around.
[*]Changed: You can now skip dialogue text animation or move to the next paragraph by clicking any key/mouse anywhere.


[*]Changed: Trading UI will only appear once the dialogue is finished. 
[*]Changed: Shortcuts are enabled when windows are open. 
[*]Changed: After battle ends, raiding (if applicable) starts after the winners celebrate, moving battle results to be viewable after raiding, viewing battle results has no countdown anymore.
[*]Changed: Units will now disengage regardless of whether the opportunity attack hit them or missed, if the opportunity attack doesn't defeat the unit, it'll move on.
[*]Changed: Minimum HP% for a unit to be eligible for battle is now 10%. 
[*]Changed: Units will now wait 1 IRL hour to lose the defeated status, then start recovering. 
[*]Changed: Encumbrance % is now represented with a bar on the unit stat list.
[*]Changed: Raids now have a two-minute timer.
[*]Changed: Looting windows will close if the looter moves while looting, this also frees the house/building to be loot-able by other players if the unit leaves it.
[*]Changed: Default unit action is changed to 'Move' if the player right clicks to cancel attack initialization to move, saving unnecessary clicks. 
[*]Changed: By standard, the Frankish Galikakus will now be deployed with his Throwing Axe as his weapon of choice, instead of his One-Handed axe. As all other units, this can be customized in the unit's Inventory by right-clicking the weapon you want and setting them as their priority.
[*]Changed: Turn duration is now 120s.
[*]Changed: Two-handed Axes now do not have Quick attacks. 
This means the only unit wielding two-handed axes, the Suebian Hildisvini (Chosen One), loses access to Quick Chop. 
We will make a new ability attack that inserts something similar to a Quick Chop; it won't be a basic attack, though, so it will need to be trained as other abilities. 
[*]Changed: Formations are disabled in random warband mode.

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]

[*]Fixed: Maxed out stats will have their spend button disabled, as well as generate no base roll bonuses.
[*]Fixed: stats and bonuses are capped accordingly while leveling up.
[*]Fixed: abilities had 0 unlock AP cost.
[*]Fixed: post battle performance window appearing empty. 
[*]Fixed: center mass restriction. 
[*]Fixed: kick description.
[*]Fixed: Hidden UI element in the middle of screen preventing clicking of certain tiles (example a deployment tile is unusable) 
[*]Fixed: Defenses (block/parry/dodge) chance calculation. 
[*]Fixed: Overlapping text in some ability descriptions. 
[*]Fixed: wrong display of no defense modifier based on proficiency.
[*]Fixed: Cleave through users will only launch a random basic melee attack if applicable. 
[*]Fixed: Missed ranged attacks hitting another unit were not working properly
[*]Fixed: units were gaining ability points when using abilities 
- Ability points are only gained when the unit levels up. 
- Basic attacks gain progress points equal to the ACP cost of performing the attack, Basic attacks level up automatically. 
- This means that free attacks cost no stamina nor count in the attack chain, but also don't contribute to the progress of the basic attack.
[*]Fixed: Breaking error when recalculating carry weight when a Baggable [cursed] item is added/removed or equipped/unequipped. 
[*]Fixed: Morale not resetting on battle end. 
[*]Fixed: Health/Stamina/Fatigue regeneration is generating every server second instead of minute. 
[*]Fixed: While above stats are regenerating, if endurance is upgraded, they were not scaled proportionally based on their current % 
[*]Fixed: An error preventing loading of saved warbands, thus forcing choosing and creating a new warband.
[*]Fixed: Charge attacks were requiring mounts to be moving to be used instead of to have gallop enabled!
[*]Fixed: Stats calculation typo resulting in stats gaining 100 points every time they're reduced. 
[*]Fixed: Breaking error when going back to lobby produced by tinkering with inventory during looting. 
[*]Fixed: All attacks were gaining 10% of stamina cost on miss, while only melee attacks should. 
[*]Fixed: Only missing required equipment will show in the tooltip instead of the full group.
[*]Fixed: Raid and Gallop not working properly Test
[*]Fixed: Stamina regeneration calculation.
[*]Fixed: Diagonal attacks not working Test
[*]Fixed: Walkable points inside Frankish Village walls. 
Fixed: Breaking error from a conflict of calculating attackable tiles (This solves diagonal calculations like long Thrust).
[*]Fixed: Several units were having maximum HP numbers lower than usual.
[*]Fixed: Overdraw shot requiring a unit to be equipping a short and long bow at the same time instead of either. 
[*]Fixed: Attacks that count as certain damage types (slashing etc...) for certain weapons were unusable. 
[*]Fixed: Abilities cooldowns were not reset for more battles in the same game session. 
[*]Fixed: A suebians deployment area on the visigoth village causing a unit to be deployed far away from its friends.
[*]Fixed: Breaking error caused by not finding the appropriate win/lose message for a tribe on certain maps causing further unexpected behavior when back to lobby. 
[*]Fixed: Some errors in morale effects events.
[*]Fixed: An error when viewing dialogues that are dependent on the unit's wielded weapon.
[*]Fixed: warbands were not being saved due to device-specific checks failing.
[*]Fixed: Ability tree icons overlapping each other or overlapping group names due to different aspect ratio from design.
All trees look exactly as per their design now. 
[*]Fixed: wrong icon for abilities that have weapon-specific icons when said weapon is no longer equipped/thrown 
- Example, a javelin icon was appearing on throw attacks when the unit runs out of throwable axes. 
Fixed: Breaking error when ignoring an opportunity attack.
[*]Fixed: Abilities/Commands with more than one turn cooldown were reset every turn.
[*]Fixed: Specialized weapon proficiency was not working.
[*]Fixed: Combat log using the actual target's name in use message instead of the selected target. 
[*]Fixed: Inventory/Equipment operations were disabled after going in a trading map. 
[*]Fixed: Some Dialogue choices were not coloring when hovered.
[*]Fixed: Effects should now be placed correctly to the corresponding unit's body, depending on the case. 
[*]Fixed: Items in bags were not tradable. 
[*]Fixed: Breaking error when querying traits for units with no traits. 
[*]Fixed: Area based passive/trait effects were not applied when the battle started unless a unit moves. 
[*]Fixed: Temporary stat effects were ignored if they were applicable instead of if they weren't.
[*]Fixed: Units that can not block/parry will not be generated with these proficiencies, nor gain xp in them.
[*]Fixed: An error where the room filter by game version was using the wrong filter key.
[*]Fixed: Breaking error when recording merchant stock in pvp based on server/build ids. 
[*]Fixed: Some short/long blades had parrying disabled.
[*]Fixed: Breaking error due to memory leak from battle map, this caused inability to view units in warband back in lobby.
[*]Fixed: Breaking error when attempting to place a throw-able weapon in a pack/holder item like a shield/quiver during battle.
[*]Fixed: A workaround to editing equipment in battle restriction by refilling the bag item with throw-able weapons while in battle.
[*]Fixed: Movement sounds were not playing the first time the unit moves. 
[*]Fixed: Error causing units to not regenerate stats.
[*]Fixed: Breaking error when displaying tile overlays for raid and gallop.
[*]Fixed: Breaking error when removing temporary effects when the caster or the receiver is defeated. 
[*]Fixed: Multiple issues with battle result window.
[*]Fixed: Stat regeneration and unit recovery making non-progressive warbands override progressive ones.
[*]Fixed: Bags were locked for addition/removal during raiding.
[*]Fixed: Some engaged units were not participating in attack commands.
[*]Fixed: Possible displacement issue due to multi unit path calculation at once(this is one of the ways I was able to reproduce the issue).
[*]Fixed: Frankish Galikakus blacking out (freezing) when switching to or from any axe animation. 
[*]Fixed: Units performing ranged attacks playing idle animation right after a ranged attack when the current state didn't really change.
[*]Fixed: Unit not playing defeated animation if health was affected by other means without playing the hurt animation, resulting in the unit staying in battle not selectable, not attackable and walkable-over.
[*]Fixed: Move button is still labeled 'disengage' after the unit defeats it's last threat, it was requiring re-selection of the unit to update. 
[*]Fixed: Attack button is highlighted even though the attack is cancelled in the background, requiring canceling/re selecting the attack.
[*]Fixed: Memory overflow error caused by wandering animal layering calculation.
[*]Fixed: Accuracy was not saved in battle history.
[*]Fixed: Attacks that were disabled after a certain attack is used were requiring re-selection of the unit to have their buttons visually disabled.
[*]Fixed: Attacks were requiring re-selection after moving with the attack list open. 
[*]Fixed: Abilities turn based cooldowns were displayed as time-based.
[*]Fixed: Automatic attacks triggered by opportunity/reaction/overpowering were not being waited for, and so 2 or more units could be attacking while the first unit's attack isn't fully done.
[*]Fixed: Presence inspiring passive effects were applied to enemies instead of friends.
[*]Fixed: Numerous errors when recording battle ending when a player forces shutdown of the game, resulted in no saving.
[*]Fixed: Trait Tough was almost present on every unit due to a testing setup.
[*]Fixed: AI was not taking into account range decay and non effective range when launching ranged attacks, resulting in very close ranged attacks.
[*]Fixed: Game freezing while an AI ranged unit is calculating it's options, the higher the unit's range the longer the freeze was, units now think in the background.
Fixed: crit multiplier rounded in display on the unit stat list.
[*]Fixed: When a learnt ability is removed from a unit's tree it wasn't removed from it's usable abilities. 
[*]Fixed: Broad Axes (Two-handed Axe class) now properly have their maximum damage accounted, instead of copying its minimum damage as maximum. 
[*]Fixed: Frame based equipment-based sound effects were skipped due to short frame time to process.
[/list]

notes.title: Welcome to 2021! Update 1.5 (test server)
notes.content:
Hello there, everyone. We started 2021 with great news. Our new update is complete, and ready for a round of testing. It was decided to not make it official until things are fully ironed out, due to the sheer amount of new content. 

To test version 1.5: 
[olist]
[*] On your Steam client, click on "Library"
[*] Right-click on "Rise of the Foederati", on the left side
[*] A new menu will pop up. Click on "Properties"
[*] Click the "Betas" tab on the new window
[*] Use the password "givememylegionsvarus", no quotes
[*] Click "Verify Code"
[*] You should see a "Code successfully verified" message.
[*] Go above, click the dropdown list and select "test server - User Beta branch"
[*] Close the new window
[*] Wait for the update to complete on the Steam client
[*] Play normally
[/olist]


Below is the changelog:

[*] Added: Support for 2v2 Battles, all members of a team must be using the same tribe.
	- If a house is being looted by another member, it is locked until they finish.
	- Team members can use Shift+Right Click Tile to send Signals to each other.
	- Team/Guild/Ally chat channel for team chat.
	- Battle statistics window will reflect all battle members performance accordingly.
	- Team members will all need to confirm deployment in order for the opponent to proceed.
        - In the future, item and units will be able to be traded between allies. This will open strategies for players dedicated to archers, cavalry, etc.
	
[*] Added: Unit progression and stat development, you can upgrade your units from the Unit Window.
	- Each unit level gives 5 stat points and 1 ability point. 
	- A unit must spend all 5 stat points to level up.
	- The more stat points spent on a stat in the previous level up, the higher the bonus gained in the next level up.
[*] Added: New Stat System and Stat Effects, hovering any stat will now show effects affecting it such as Traits/Passive or Temporary Effects in battle.
[*] Added: Fumbled effect, fumbled units have their damage, accuracy and block/dodge/parry/cover halved till their next attack. A fumble occurs when a unit scores less than 5.00 on his attack roll.
[*] Added: Disoriented effect, disoriented units have their block/dodge/parry/cover values halved.
[*] Added: Health, Stamina and Fatigue regeneration for units post battle, for every minute off battle health regenerates 1%, fatigue -1%, and stamina 5%. Items will be able to be used to speed up regeneration drastically.
[*] Added: Traits and Passives that affect a unit's authority points/deployment cost have their effects shown when hovering.
[*] Added: Traits and Passives that affect units opinions of each other.
[*] Added: Trait opinion effects of leaders when the trait owner is deployed/not deployed.
[*] Added: Trait Morale Loss/Gain Resistance effects that prevent morale loss/gain for certain stacks based on the trait.
[*] Added: Proper combat message for critical hits.
[*] Added: Chance to ignore attacks of opportunity by traits, units that ignore attacks of opportunity can regenerate 10% of their missing stamina.
[*] Added: Chance to nullify critical hits.
[*] Added: Critical Miss, units that critically miss in their last turn will have a chance of being automatically hit by some abilities.
[*] Added: Doors to several Suebian Village houses.
[*] Added: Cliffs. Elevations now serve only as an obstacle. In the future, bonuses to ranged attackers on higher terrain and penalties to ranged attackers on lower terrain will be given. Certain abilities will be more/less effective against a strategy of holding an elevated position.
[*] Added: Buffs that recover stamina/fatigue.
[*] Added: Ability to deactivate target retaliation if hit by a charge attack.
[*] Added: Some charges will be disabled against some reactions.
[*] Added: Support for distance based leader command effects (A command will apply effects to units at different distances).
[*] Added: Poison-like effect some abilities will cause units to lose a percentage of their HP on hit and next turn.
[*] Added: Some attacks will not count in the attack chain nor cost stamina depending on the ability or the circumstance it was used.
[*] Added: Support to incur loss to target's movement range on attacking its feet. Several abilities prompt this effect.
[*] Added: Support for Pacing abilities effects and Pacing stacks, also changed Pacing ability type to work as intended.
[*] Added: Support for passives that affect other units when engaging/using specific attack or against certain attacks.
[*] Added: Toggle effects that disable critical hit for melee/ranged attacks.
[*] Added: Certain toggles may detoggle if a unit takes damage.

[*] Fixed: Blocking is not enabled for weapons that are melee&ranged alike.
[*] Fixed: Attacks that launch at the target more than once like Overwhelm/Overpower work properly now.
[*] Fixed: An error when viewing descriptions of locked abilities.
[*] Fixed: Rounding issues for attributes like Movement Points, Movement Range and Attack Chain Points that were causing inconsistent behaviour.
[*] Fixed: Encumberance row on the unit stat list will now show the value calculated properly.
[*] Fixed: Disabled buttons will no longer play the click sound when clicked.
[*] Fixed: A bug in deployment where if a player choses to end deployment without enough cavalry/rangers, the deployed units are not synced.
[*] Fixed  AI freezing in deployment sometimes if units fail to look at the enemy's deployment area.
[*] Fixed: An error when opening ability tree for units with deprecated/deleted abilities.
[*] Fixed: Stats rows are glitching and overlapping in the unit window sometimes.
[*] Fixed: An eror when removing a defeated unit from engagement with its threats.

[*] Changed: Cavalry units now require gallop to be enabled to charge.
[*] Changed: Some attacks will only be usable if the unit has less/more than half its movement points.
[*] Changed: Loot in almost every single house in the game has been redone and rebalanced. Most old maps did not have possible loot for coins.
[*] Changed: Dialogue choices that will result in no further dialogues in Encampment, will return to lobby immediately.
[*] Changed: Removed delay when showing next dialogue after picking a choice.
[*] Changed: Dialogue choice color will change if hovered.
[*] Changed: If a random warband is not used in a battle (battle cancelled in lobby or deployment) the warband is not destroyed and is still usable.

notes.title: Update 1.4.1
notes.content:
Hello guys, Many new changes and fixes on this update. We are aware of other bugs and other problems related to dialogues and we're working hard to fix them. As it stands now, our focus on development will be on the items of our timeline, namely 2v2 battles, tournaments, a ranked system and most importantly, a simple territory control type of game that will be used in the future for our big online mode. This should take some time, and meanwhile smaller but also important updates such as new tribes and units are also in the mix. 

As we stated earlier this year, we want to push for a more standarized update system that fixes things and gets published every week, but because these are bigger things, we might delay the updates next month, especially with Christmas coming.

notes.title: Update 1.4.0
notes.content:
Hi everyone. It is with great pleasure that we announce our next big update for Rise of the Foederati, with plenty of improvements, changes and game additions that once again are padding the way for our bigger projects. This is probably the last big update before our next step in the project for our first tournaments and ranked plays. More than ever maintaining and keeping your warband in top shape will be required to make your tribe trail in to victory. More details will follow in the future. Here are the changes for this new version:

[list]
[*] Added: Suebian Village map. A semi-closed village that has two groups fighting in the chokepoint in the entrance, similar to the Franks. This is a larger village that will require players to choose a side to loot, and you are unable to loot everything on purpose; the objective is to make several tries until you can have the best looting pathway, until we implement drop-in battles against players looting a village mid-way.

[*] Added: Warband window now allows zooming of units with the middle-button of the mouse.

[*] Added: Small block effect for units with shields that previously did not have it, making it more consistent.

[*] Added: "Talk" function for all your soldiers. Almost all soldiers you talk to have different dialogues which can yield different answers from a list. Soon we'll add more dialogue options for more units.

[*] Added: An encampment for your units. When talking to your units, you will go to your encampment. In the future, different types of infrastructure amenities will change the scene, leading to many configurations ranging from a small camp for your few men to full-range large camps divided by divisions.

[*] Changed: Bow, Spear and Javelin icons now have a white outline to make them more visible in inventories.

[*] Changed: Strong attacks now deal less damage, but cost less Stamina. This is made to prevent damage spikes.

[*] Fixed: Warband window should now have consistent miniatures of the soldiers.

[*]Fixed: Obstacles (trees/buildings) sometimes weren't turning transparent unless a certain part was hovered.

[*]Fixed: "Sunk" tree on Basques Village map.

[*]Fixed: Suebian Leader had wrong idle static sprite.

[*]Fixed: Short Bows were being generated with 0 minimum damage.

[*]Fixed: Small animation fix in Frankish Baro's blocking animation.

[*]Fixed: Frankish Heerbanni now should properly have a block effect on their shields.

[*]Fixed: Basque and Frankish Village now should be properly lootable.
[/list]

Have fun! We're still keeping our poll up, Two tribes are fighting for the top, and it is an almost-tie. If you would like to help us more, check the link below and vote for what tribe you'd like next:

surveyhero.com/c/21a5b339

notes.title: Merchants, Currency, Looting, Leaderboards and +
notes.content:
Hello there.

Development has been made on the merchant system, where players can buy weapons, supplies and general items to aid them in combat, and sell their hard-earned loot. This is all adaptations to our current system which was devised to showcase our game, as we move closer to the final World Campaign mode. 

When finished, in your Warband scene, you will be able to choose between travelling to a Wandering Merchant, Blacksmith or to the nearby Marketplace. Each merchant sells and buys specific items.

[b]Marketplace:[/b] Here you buy supplies such as food, alcohol, tools and medical items. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/c96d0cb7ec76cdfbae943ba0b8b18e48e220a51d.png[/img]

[b]Wandering Merchant: [/b] This rootless, travelling merchant will buy off your loot and also sell items with a high mark-up, but sometimes he may have weapons, armor or something which you won't be able to find elsewhere. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/40afbee93e92ee92022f001729bf074c432b38e6.png[/img]

[b]Blacksmith: [/b] The local blacksmith will buy off from you armor, weapons, hides and scrap metal from you. Obviously, he also sells ammunition, armor, shields, helmets, weapons and everything needed to keep your warband well-supplied.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/30bc88f6e190d609b39f3150458d71f147420e7d.png[/img]

We will have more merchants in the future, such as a Horse Breeder, for example. These are just the first three to get our trading system going. There will be some livelihood to the trading scene, as villagers and their children roam around the roads to simulate the populace of the town you're trading in, and this will later come in handy for us to populate the villages, so its not just a personal touch.

Second, we are re-evaluating our current currency system to involve more physical currencies. notes.title: Update 1.3.0
notes.content:
Hi everyone. With some more delays, and a few hiccups, we managed to deliver our second big update for Rise of the Foederati. Contrary to the first, we decided to opt for a test server launch before putting it live, for security and testing reasons. Here are the instructions on how to play 1.3.0:

[olist]
[*] On your Steam client, click on "Library"
[*] Right-click on "Rise of the Foederati", on the left side
[*] A new menu will pop up. Click on "Properties"
[*] Click the "Betas" tab on the new window
[*] Use the password "suebianssuebians", no quotes
[*] Click "Verify Code"
[*] You should see a "Code successfully verified" message.
[*] Go above, click the dropdown list and select "test server - User Beta branch"
[*] Close the new window
[*] Wait for the update to complete on the Steam client
[*] Play normally
[/olist]

Everything going smoothly, we expect this test server to last for about a couple weeks, while we iron out the new mechanics and possible new bugs. Finally, below is the list of what's new in 1.3.0.

[list]
[*]Added: New tribe; the Suebians. A Germanic tribe with roots on the shores of the Albis (Elbe) river. Their wandering and constant shifting in territories led them to reach the western area of Hispania. An infantry-centric tribe with incredible tenacity in combat, these rugged warriors adapted well to their lives in their new lands, borrowing several martial concepts from their neighbours.

[*]Added: New music for pre-engagement and post-engagement phases. Won't spoil the surprise here on how many they are; play to find them out!

[*]Added: Quality modifiers for weapons. Weapons of better quality will usually have better performance. Because durability mechanics are not implemented yet, most mid-level qualities will have no difference between themselves. Not every weapon you'll find has a quality modifier; we want to check whether the current modifiers are not displacing too much power division amongst a lower and a higher quality weapon; expect more to be added in future updates as we at the same time balance current modifiers.

[*]Added: Charge mechanics. Units that run/gallop more than half of their remaining movement to attack will deal extra damage, but will also take extra damage from Counters. When commanded to charge, all units will do it in unison, creating a morale debilitation effect against the enemy, especially if the charge attack hits. It goes without saying, cavalry units deal even more damage in charges, but can become vulnerable to counter-attacks if surrounded.

[*]Added: Ride-by attack mechanics. Most cavalry units now can use a toggle ability which when turned on (requires them to be galloping), will make them attack the first unit they enter in contact while galloping, and keep moving while ignoring engagement locks. These attacks are more inaccurate than charges, but can deal good damage while maintaining cavalry out of harm's way.

[*]Added: Frankish Village map. A more organized tribal settlement, occupied and built from an old station house in the plains of Belgica; the Roman-styled house contrast with the other homesteads built by the Franks.

[*]Added: New armor type: Hides. Most hide-based armor are a mid-way between Light and Medium armor in protection, having overall balanced protection amongst all damage types, with special focus on reducing Smashing damage. It is also the second heaviest type of armor, even being heavier than several metal-based Medium armor models.

[*]Added: New weapon types; One-handed Hammers and Two-handed Axes. Hammers deal Smashing damage, which is hard to protect against and also are much cheaper than other weapon types. Cruder hammers like wooden clubs can be considered ubiqutous,. However, they are tiring to wield and heavy. Two-handed Axes are tough-to-master weapons because of their large Stamina cost per attack and low critical chances, but a good critical hit can deal outstanding amounts of damage.

[*]Added: Tooltip showing expected damage and attack being used. Expected Damage uses the prerrogative that the target enemy is wearing no armor; armored enemies will most probably not receive the displayed damage, as the reduction will be taken into account.

[*]Changed: Several item icons now have a white outline and/or better presentation to help their visualization when looting.

[*]Changed: All Light Spears now grant a buff called "Double Grip" when wielded with both hands. Double Grip grants +3 bonus Damage, +0.25x Critical Hit Multipliers and +3 Critical Hit Damage Added. The bonus in the future will shift and change according to the model of spear used, meaning certain spears may be more useful than others to be wielded this way. Several abilities in the future will require this buff to be on, but for now, only two units benefit from this; the Visigoth Horseman and Frankish Rider. Basque Lance Cavalry units use Heavy Spears, so are unaffected by this change, since all Heavy Spears already require two hands to be wielded.

[*]Fixed: Spying on enemy units now does not show the window offscreen.
[/list]

Intensive work will follow to make this update as stable as possible for a live version. Expect new updates soon. Last, but not least, thank you for the patience, as usual. Have fun!

notes.title: Regarding Update 1.3.0
notes.content:
Hello there, its been a while since we posted any new events or news regarding developing. We have a bunch of things ready for release, and additional things that aren't exactly visual for you players, but definately helps our development in the long run. This is going to be a big patch, which is going to be available in a test server first. 

Here's what is ready:

[list]
[*] A much-requested "Surrender" function to speed up battles.

[*] 80% of the Suebians units are fully animated. 

[*] Charge attacks and ride-by attacks of cavalry units, further exploring their mobility in the game.

[*] The core coding for markets.

[*] Quality modifiers for weapons/armor
[/list]

And here's what we're coding and developing, and once ready, will be posted in the test server:

[list]
[*] A basic first list of items for markets for sale.

[*] A few Suebian units still being animated.

[*] Ambient sounds 

[*] New map: Frankish Village.

[*] Quality modifiers for shields
[/list]

After 1.3.0, our focus will go into 1.3.1, which will feature the Suebian Village map, the continuation of coding for unit development and better game mode selections. We are aware several items previously requested are not in those lists, and may or may not get into either update. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/89dd06ce132e10d3f3e6a28cf044ebeab9a9d257.png[/img]

Our estimate date for 1.3.0 is late July, but may be earlier. Following our timeline, there will also be some focus on creating a competitive game mode for territorial conquest; the maps for this game mode are being made as we speak. There are things we are doing earlier than expected, and other things may be pushed a month or two; such is the nature of timelines, and there'll be an update regarding it soon, so people know what we delivered and what's getting ready or not, with all due transparency.

Thank you for your support and your patience.

notes.title: Update 1.2.0
notes.content:
Hello there, we have been working, and this is the second big update for the game. We decided to call it 1.2.0 due to the amount of background networking changes and improvements. Because of the amount of problems of the old systems, there was a need to make everything from the ground up, and our programmer decided to do exactly that. Next updates will also be crucial for the game, opening spaces for more intricate mechanics. 

It is taking longer than expected to make the unit development coding, since most of our time was used to stabilize player vs player networking, so please apologize our delay. If all things go well from this update on, we might be able to catch up to our timeline in a month or two.

[list]
[*] Added: Difficulty levels for PVE, difficulty level affects the generated AI's warband equipment quality, units levels, weapon/defense proficiencies (currently, more difficult battles means the enemy will deploy more levelled units with better equipment).

[*] Changed: Buffs/Debuffs Icons are grouped by source now.

[*] Changed: AI warband is always fresh (Non-Progressive) and it reflects the difficulty level selected.

[*] Changed: Networking infrastructure is revamped to fix multiple performance, delays and syncing issues.

[*] Changed: Slightly reduced sounds of horses when moving in trot speed. Galloping remains unchanged (effectively making galloping a horse louder, as it should be)

[*] Changed: Rain sounds should be more subtle.

[*] Fixed: Basque Lancer units were moving too slowly.

[*] Fixed: Small jilting in Basque Lancer's Idle animation

[*] Fixed: Map descriptions for the Franks.

[*] Fixed: Ranged weapon's attacks information like range and range decay were not shown in examine panel for weapons that are melee and ranged like Javelins.

[*] Fixed: Authority points were using wrong calculations against the unit's charisma.

[*] Fixed: Damage was always being clamped to 1/4 its value (probably the reason why battles were taking so long).
[/list]

notes.title: Update 1.1.9
notes.content:
Hi, we have been working. Thanks to our event this weekend, many inconsistencies were fixed, and one of the most common complaints people have on combat is addressed on disengaging mechanics. Shielded units now are less defensive, but will tire units less when they block.


[list]
[*]Added: New disengage mechanic, units engaged can now move with the following rules:
        -Disengaging will trigger attacks of opportunity from enemy engaged units.
        -If an unit activates a reactive ability, it cannot disengage in the same turn (it is possible to first disengage, then activate a reactive ability).
        -If any attack of opportunities hit, the disengage is cancelled, and the unit loses half of its movement points and two ACPs, if available.
        -A unit has one disengagement attempt per turn.
        -In the future, cavalry units will be able to disengage even if attacks of opportunity hit.

[*]Changed: battle map is now scrollable by moving the mouse to the edges.

[*]Changed: some optimizations to the in-game chat UI.

[*]Changed: Shields now use less stamina to block melee attacks, but have their block and cover values reduced slightly.

[*]Fixed: Cavalry units were not launching opportunity attacks in PVP mode.

[*]Fixed: Sprint/Gallop not synced in PVP mode.

[*]Fixed: Flanking arrow indicator of the unit was invisible when the unit moves or when alone.

[*]Fixed: movement sound not looping.

[*]Fixed: attack discontinuation and timing out.

PS: We will post modifications to the AI's play to handle disengaging and improve their functionality (this will make PvE matches harder).
[/list]

notes.title: Update 1.1.8 and Hotfix 1.1.8b
notes.content:
Hello there, we have been working, and during testing this new update, we forgot to add an important fix to stamina rulesets. So this event regards both the update and its hotfix, and here are the list of changes:

[list]
[*]Added: Hotkeys for basic attacks 1-X where X is the count of basic attacks in the shown list, PS: attack list must be visible for the hotkeys to work.

[*]Added: Units now are generated with different levels of attack and defense proficiencies. If their level is above 1, they get additional proficiency. This changes drastically from unit to unit. This is another step forward to unit development. Combat should be more dynamic and with less misses in general, since proficiencies increase accuracy.

[*]Added: Floating texts for stamina and morale changes to the player's own units.

[*]Changed: Critical hit chance is now clamped to the weapon's basic critical hit if the unit's accuracy is not high enough (in a nutshell this means that on extremely low accuracy checks will do less critical hits)

[*]Changed: When a player performs an attack or uses an ability, the current ability list will not close unless said attack/ability ended the unit's turn.

[*]Changed: Shortcuts are now disabled when a UI window is open in battle.

[*]Changed: Selected attack icon should have a better effect now.

[*]Changed: When attempting to use an unusable attack for the moment, a better message is displayed to reflect the reason.

[*]Changed: Attack rolls are now displayed with two decimal cases for better readability.

notes.title: Update 1.1.0 - The Franks
notes.content:
Hi there. We finally concluded [u]this round of [/u]development and here's what's new:

[h3]New tribe: The Franks[/h3]

You will be able to choose them from the tribes roster, summing now up to three choices. Currently, the Franks have one leader, the Baron (Baro), a Medium Infantry unit that can take some punishment and command the frontlines, either countering cavalry with his spear or hacking enemies with his axe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/5db50a74d5194e0756eeab2081947f94c0f3a446.png[/img]

The tribe has two options as cavalry; the Rider (Ridanmanne) is a cheap, Light Cavalry unit that can disrupt the enemy's backline and support the rest of the group. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/d35b054618abe230b7e707ba6d415b2f1aace72e.png[/img]

The other cavalry unit, the Cavalryman (Hundesridan), wears mail armor, helmet and shield, being exceptionally tougher than other cavalry units and able to keep pressuring in melee combat with his sword, while having a wicked charge with a backup spear.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/f097d4862b2d96d7914d9829cfe242ab600b857b.png[/img]

The two infantry choices are the Levy Warrior (Heerbaan), a Light Infantryman carrying an axe for melee and some for ranged combat, which makes it not only a cheap unit, but also quite flexible to soften enemy ranks before going into melee.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/0b18750a92922ee14c15f7919776beee130329a3.png[/img]

Alternatively, you might also want more professional soldiers. In this case, you can deploy the Retainer (Trustismanne), highly skilled swordsmen that are considered Medium Infantry units, while being quick and lethal in melee combat. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/07db3fd21f73fdb3253dba154cb65a1a13cb8400.png[/img]

Finally, the Franks are not keen on using bows in combat. Their ranged warriors are the Axe Throwers (Galikakum), which may lack range when compared to bowmen, but can dish out large damage in medium-to-close range, while also being cheap to field and much more dangerous in melee with their backup axe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/dfe8f07cc066f337e709cac1541a47d573c9b694.png[/img]


[h3]Ability Trees[/h3]

We have started to implement ability trees. Most units now have two ability paths which they can choose when levelling up. You will notice that one path is blank; in the future, all units will gain three paths which build up their training in and out of combat, giving players choices to specialize their soldiers. Two identical units may be different in stat builds, abilities, skills and traits, and in the future, their skin might also be different, summing up to lots of personalization in units. 

Please take note that some abilities will be bugged, or outright not work. We are still working to make everything available and go smoothly. 

[h3]Patch Notes[/h3]

Finally, these are the patch notes. Be aware that this patch will reset your current warband and all loot you've acquired so far. 

Fixed: Command: Preserve now correctly animates and triggers the right sound.
Fixed: some projectiles looping the hit sound while airborne.
Replaced: placeholder messages on battle beginning
Fixed: multiple localization bugs.
Fixed: error thrown when visiting The Franks page in encyclopedia from tribe selection screen.
Fixed exception thrown when trying to get effects of an ability level higher than the ability’s max level.
Fixed: out of memory exception when generating map loots.
Fixed: critical hit morale changes not taking into account the nature of the source attack.
Fixed: errors thrown when toggling tabs in these windows (Battle Results, Warband Logistics, Warband Supplies and Chat tabs).
Fixed: online playercounter updates continuously and less overhead.
Fixed: error thrown because Pine Forest doesn't support looting.
Fixed: memory leaks because map grid data was not cleaned up once player leaves the map.
Fixed: when a unit is defeated while playing idle animation, it played defeat animation directly, skipping hurt animation.
Added: unit's class and rarity to the unit's tooltip.
Fixed: multiple notifications about player leaving room resulting in an exception after the first notification.
Fixed: crash when attempting to render a unit with no applicable stance or unknown deployability reason.
Fixed: an exception when checking if two units are/were adjacent and one of them was defeated.
Fixed: an exception thrown when attempting to interact with empty inventory slots.
Fixed: inventory manpiulation data sync big size, it is now lightweight and only changes are synced.
Fixed: warband generation causing freeze and possible infinite loops, it is now instant, saving still depends on your internet.
Fixed: movement of an item to the same inventory resulting in a freeze.
Fixed: unit slot throwing an error on leaving map.

Currently, the Franks have one leader, the Baron (Baro), a Medium Infantry unit that can take some punishment and command the frontlines, either countering cavalry with his spear or hacking enemies with his axe.
The tribe has two options as cavalry; the Rider (Ridanmanne) is a cheap, Light Cavalry unit that can disrupt the enemy's backline and support the rest of the group.

The other cavalry unit, the Cavalryman (Hundesridan), wears mail armor, helmet and shield, being exceptionally tougher than other cavalry units and able to keep pressuring in melee combat with his sword, while having a wicked charge with a backup spear.

The two infantry choices are the Levy Warrior (Heerbaan), a Light Infantryman carrying an axe for melee and some for ranged combat, which makes it not only a cheap unit, but also quite flexible to soften enemy ranks before going into melee.

Alternatively, you might also want more professional soldiers. In this case, you can deploy the Retainer (Trustismanne), highly skilled swordsmen that are considered Medium Infantry units, while being quick and lethal in melee combat.

Finally, the Franks are not keen on using bows in combat. Their ranged warriors are the Axe Throwers (Galikakum), which may lack range when compared to bowmen, but can dish out large damage in medium-to-close range, while also being cheap to field and much more dangerous in melee with their backup axe.
We have started to implement ability trees. Most units now have two ability paths which they can choose when levelling up.
You will notice that one path is blank; in the future, all units will gain three paths which build up their training in and out of combat, giving players choices to specialize their soldiers.
Two identical units may be different in stat builds, abilities, skills and traits, and in the future, their skin might also be different, summing up to lots of personalization in units.
