notes.title: News on development
notes.content:
Hello there. 

As we approach our goal of adding the truckload of content being worked on, there are plenty of points to be discussed, mainly regarding the new ability trees and comeback of units using abilities for combat, which greatly increases the complexity of combat.

A French website also wrote a cool review of our game, which is very well-done and showcases the strengths (and weaknesses) of our current state of the game. Overall, it shows that most of our objectives this early on development were archieved, at least for the reviewer in question. We are always open for discussions about how the game progresses, obviously.

(translated to English)
https://translate.google.com.br/translate?sl=auto&tl=en&u=https%3A%2F%2Fdystopeek.fr%2Fjouer%2Fjv%2Fearly-access-rise-of-the-foederati%2F

[h2]Regarding abilities[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/d9c69c5123894da7293c071d708ddc2736a664cc.png[/img]

There are currently about 100 abilities pre-coded and ready to be released for this patch. However, because there are many milestones to be met this month, we will probably settle with half of the abilities ready for launch, and the other half requiring fine-tuning, balancing and/or hardcoding to be used. Judging by our current roster of 12 units to be expanded to 18, and several units having the same abilities, it should be enough to cover enough ability choices for two ability tree paths. This means we will push for a new tribe update with two ability tree paths for unit customization. 

Our aim for ability icons should be close to what we have for basic attacks, and because this is a heavy investment from our point of view, placeholders will be used. As our development continues, these placeholders will slowly be replaced by our own textures, so we ask patience for the players that will see conflicting textures for their abilities and basic attacks. The good part of that is it allows faster implementation of abilities. Old icons we used for older builds will take priority in replacement.

[h2]Unit development[/h2]

Something that will be a constant in the game is unit development, not only in combat, but also in training. Because our warband management is not a priority now, there are several things that need to be completed for a more well-fleshed out development of your units. For now, the simple idea of making units fight to level up will be there, and in the future, balancing more veteran units against each other to prevent newbies being crushed by those who are already playing since the beginning will be something to be kept an eye on, until a matchmaking system is implemented better. Our objective is to make even a newly created player be a threat to a veteran, if he plays well and knows how to tactically overpower the more levelled player. 

However, we also believe power of troops can make newbie players level up fast; so players will not be as annoyed to be defeated by players with units too levelled; the experience gain will skyrocket. After the next patch, our priority will be implemented experience to units, so you can develop your warband as you play.

[h2]The Franks[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/99b19c42bfedd6fe2de945ee864fdfe159585585.jpg[/img]

The new tribe needs several tweaks on animations, graphics and obviously, will be implemented with their ability trees ready. This is a quite different tribe in that the only ranged unit is an axethrower. Their cavalry so far has a light and medium alternative, and infantry-wise, they do not have armored soldiers (for now), with the exception of their leader, a Medium-infantry unit with enough tanking to be almost considered a Heavy infantry unit. It should be interesting to see how players will react to a leader that is extremely resillient, and is still not even considered a Heavy Infantry unit. 

Our timeline expected the new tribe to be launched in April, considering a launch also in the same month. Since we launched in early May, we are trying to compress our goals to keep it consistent, and launch it this month while we make a code cleanup. It's also important to note many of our goals, like the ones below, are not implemented in the timeline, so many things not pointed there are being worked on by us.

[h2]Economy[/h2]

You need to sell your loot! After this update, we will develop a merchant feature in warband management, where you can sell and buy things at a very reasonable price (or not, depending on what you want). This feature, as most we are implementing, will be much better fleshed out in the future, but will already give players an idea of what we want when it comes to looting, selling and buying goods, weapons and supplies.

[h2]Warband management[/h2]

Wounds are nearly ready for implementation, and will probably be pushed for the next update after this one. After battle, your units will carry on their HP, Fatigue and Stamina. Players need to rest and treat their own units to become available again, or wait until their HP/Fatigue resets. This feature is going to be much more intricate than this, but a simpler system will be present for players, until then. Medical items are implemented, but do not do anything yet. 

Food and alcohol are also supplies players need to gather for their marches in-game. For now, since we only have battles, warbands only need to make sure they have alcohol and food for everyone. Because the merchant will not have all types of drinks or food available at all times, making sure you are well-supplied with a good variety of food and alcohol is a great way to keep your men with good morale.

[h2]Our Discord[/h2]

If you have any questions to us regarding the game, or just any subject, we highly encourage you to open a thread on the Steam discussion hub. But since not everyone has the patience to do so, we can also be accessed through our social media links and Discord server. Below is a link you can join. 

https://discord.gg/zdfSds8


Last, but not least, we do not have a clear date to push our next update, but this weekend should be very busy. Regardless of updates, we will keep trying to at the very least post updates regarding game development once a week.

notes.title: Coming soon: The Franks
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37607287/99b19c42bfedd6fe2de945ee864fdfe159585585.jpg[/img]

For those wondering who are the warriors in the game's Library header, consider your curiosity sated today. As announced in our timeline, we will add the third tribe in Rise of the Foederati soon, the Franks. Considered to be one of the closest barbarian allies of Rome, the Franks in a previous time were composed of minor clans and two major denominations, called the Ripuarians and Salians. The first are mainly former Roman soldiers who settled in the region of the Rhenus (modern Rhein) river, deserters of Roman soldier ranks and allied tribesmen near the urban centers, while the Salians are the more brutal and warlike men from the coastal regions, forged by fire under the naval raids of Scandinavian raiders. From this more powerful side rose Merovech, a former chieftain so successful in fending off the Huns, uniting the clans and aiding the Romans that today he is considered by many to be descendant of gods. 

[previewyoutube=2ir_0QSz5uM;full][/previewyoutube]

If you are looking for flying axes, powerful cavalry and unwielding, gritty leaders, look no further than the Franks to be your tribe of choice.

In another note, I'd like to thank all the people who supported our project by purchasing our early access. This first week has been very fulfilling for the team, proving that although we have a very, very long road ahead, the path we trailed so far seems to be leading us to the correct destination. 

- Alan

notes.title: Update 1.0.2
notes.content:
Hello everyone, we officially launched our first update here. Details are below:

V 1.0.2

* This build will reset your current warband.

Shortcuts:
	- screenshot shortcut in game Ctrl+Alt+S
	- manual feature or bug report window Shift+Alt+B

Tribe Selection:
	- Videos will not play by default.
	- Clicking a video's thumbnail will play it in full view.
	- Added Basques and visigoth's maps images.

Traits:
	- Fixed traits stats and descriptions.
	- Units get assigned 1-5 traits on generation.

UI:
	- Fixed: locked abilities will not show in ability list in combat.
	- Fixed: damage type's name of a weapon item not displaying properly in item's examine panel.
	- Fixed: Inventory item's quality glow not appearing sometimes.
	- Added: better, more organized stats list, values also take into account equipped items, like shields, weapons etc.
	- Fixed: tooltip not anchored to some UI elements properly.
	- Fixed: some units icons in warband are not centered to the slot.
	- Fixed: a crash when attempting to show battle results with no previous battle history.
	- Added: current level progress to the unit's tooltip.
	
	
Added: automatic bug reporter.

Group Stash:
	- Increased capacity in group stash to 200 slots.
	- Increased size of the window.

Maps:
	- Fixed some grass not visible by default.
	- Pine Forest (new map):
		- Added more deployment areas.
		- Fixed pine trees not fading to show behind units.
	
Added: Battle classification, each battle has classification when viewing its results in results window. Classifications can bring a unit xp penalty or bonus; winning a 

difficult battle brings more experience than an easy one. Losing a difficult battle brings less penalties.
	- Sole Survival Win: Player wins, with only one unit left. (bonus 100 % XP for the unit that survived)
	- Phyrrhic Win: Player wins but loses 75 % or more of their units. (bonus 40% XP for units)
	- Close Loss: Player loses, but defeats 75 % or more of the enemy. (bonus 25% XP for units)
	- Loss: Player loses, but defeats some units. (5% XP penalty)
	- Total Loss: Player loses without defeating any unit. (10% XP penalty)
	- win: Player wins, but loses some units. (bonus 15% XP)
	- Clear Win: Player wins, only loses one unit (if battle has 20 or more units, only loses 1 or 2 units). (bonus 5% XP)
	- Total Win: Player wins and loses no units. (bonus 10% XP for units)


Added: units gain xp on battle end, if opponent disconnects, the enemy units gains some XP but not that of a win.
Fixed: a crash when initializing units on some devices if the unit is rendered before initialization.
Fixed: units were undeployable because of API upgrade.
Fixed: Wrong Icon (Unit Stance) for Boga Aihwudrauhts.
Fixed: mounted units not playing correct movement sfx.
Fixed: some units not regenerating MP and ACP on new turns and thus unable to move.

Ability Tree: as planned, we have added the foundations for ability trees for units. You can customize the training of each unit, picking abilities which may seem best fit for your group. Certain combinations will give you better mileage in each section of the game.

Some trees will not have any effect for now, at least until we implement more features (such as unit opinions, hunger/alcohol needs, map bonuses). This is intentional. If you want to be more of a min/maxer player at this stage of the game, it is not recommended that you train in those branches.

	- Each unit has an ability tree now.
	- By default all basic attacks of the unit are unlocked.
	- By default some commands for leaders are unlocked.
	- Open abilities tab in character window to access ability tree.
	

We plan to update at the very least once per week, but major bugs and exceptions can be made throughout development.
